FALSIFIER: Core diagnosis-to-action logic, remediation chains, or config touched by immune actions lie outside the extracted range.

FINDING_ID: PF003  
ASSUMPTION: Round 0 can still be called “blind” while giving models the 6 convergent findings.  
FALSIFIER: Prior findings anchor the review or suppress independent rediscovery/challenge.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS — this is seeded validation, not blind discovery.  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
REVISION: Split Round 0 into `R0a` true blind discovery and `R0b` seeded validation, or rename the current round to “seeded validation.”

FINDING_ID: PF004  
ASSUMPTION: The 1,200-line immune slice is uniformly manageable for all models as a single prompt.  
FALSIFIER: The actual prompt exceeds existing per-model context/dispatch thresholds.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS — the selected code slice is ~52,593 chars before wrapper text or seeded findings; DeepSeek is always decomposed and Codex has a 60k threshold in [run_exp12_live_wire.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp12_live_wire.py):754.  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
REVISION: Codify per-model dispatch policy: DeepSeek pre-decomposed by default, threshold fallback for Codex/ChatGPT, full-scope only when the final prompt stays under threshold.

FINDING_ID: PF005  
ASSUMPTION: The success criteria are discriminative enough to prove the experiment succeeded for the immune layer.  
FALSIFIER: The criteria can be satisfied without new immune-layer validation.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS — “all 6 convergent findings resolved” is already nearly pre-satisfied by the draft, and “3 models survive to round 3+” can be confounded by transport/context policy rather than immune correctness.  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
REVISION: Replace with revalidation criteria: the 6 prior resolutions still hold under current code, at least 3 productive model streams produce parseable output through round 3, and immune-triggered scenarios behave as expected.

FINDING_ID: PF006  
ASSUMPTION: The ascending abstraction guard will demonstrably fire during the live experiment.  
FALSIFIER: The run terminates for another reason, or the reviewed slice never produces a rising-abstraction sequence.  
ASSESSMENT: UNCERTAIN — the guard exists in code, but this plan does not force the conditions needed to exercise it.  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
REVISION: Add a deterministic replay or synthetic scenario that creates an ascending-abstraction pattern and proves the guard blocks stop.

FINDING_ID: PF007  
ASSUMPTION: Cross-model agreement is an appropriate verification gate for proposed fixes.  
FALSIFIER: Multiple models independently converge on the same wrong claim.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS — agreement is useful corroboration, but it is not verification.  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
REVISION: Use cross-model agreement only for prioritisation; accept or reject fixes via code trace plus failing-before/passing-after test, or explicit proof for `NO FIX NEEDED`.

FINDING_ID: PF008  
ASSUMPTION: Load balancing can stay out of scope except for a light interface mention.  
FALSIFIER: Immune diagnoses materially depend on benching, decomposition, dispatch blocking, or post-round role changes.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS — the immune layer reasons about active model count, benching distortion, dispatch false positives, pre-decomposition, and post-round reassignment; the current plan under-specifies those interfaces.  
SEVERITY: 0.85  
REVISION: Keep Area 2 out of the primary defect harvest, but add mandatory interface scenarios covering bench/unbench, feasibility block then decomposition success, and role reassignment after immune-triggered failures.

### OPEN QUESTION RESPONSES

Q1: Pre-decompose DeepSeek. That matches the existing runner behavior and avoids a predictable prompt-size failure. Keep full-scope review for CC2 and Gemini, allow ChatGPT full-scope unless context grows too large, and give Codex a threshold fallback because the selected slice plus context is already near its existing limit.

Q2: Do not provide the 6 convergent findings in the blind round. Run a true blind pass first, then a seeded validation pass. That preserves independent discovery signal and still lets Experiment 17 explicitly retest the old fixes.

Q3: Keep `immune_damping_rounds = 2`. It matches the default 2-round remediation verification window in [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py):3033, which is the simplest sufficient setting: `1` is too twitchy, `3` slows escalation too much for a short experiment.

Q4: Test load balancing separately, but not invisibly. Keep Experiment 17 primarily immune-focused and add explicit interface probes for load-balancing effects. Full joint scope will blur attribution; zero interface testing will miss real immune failure modes.

### PROPOSED IMPROVEMENTS

IMP001: Expand the extracted code boundaries to the true operational boundaries of the immune layer, not the current truncated line windows.

IMP002: Add a two-stage Round 0: `blind discovery` then `seeded validation of prior convergent findings`.

IMP003: Add an appendix-to-code traceability table for `f_del`, `η_dec`, `φ_i`, false-positive rate, chain exhaustion, damping, and self-diagnosis, with each item mapped to code or marked “not exercised in Exp17”.

IMP004: Add deterministic replay scenarios for `kappa stuck`, `findings decline`, `dispatch false positive`, `model failure`, and `ascending abstraction guard`, so success does not depend on a live run happening to trigger them.

IMP005: Add a per-model dispatch matrix to the plan, including whether decomposed models count toward convergence and success metrics.

IMP006: Change fix handling to `AUTO | DEFER | NO-FIX`, run targeted immune tests first, then the full suite, and require human approval for structural or multi-model prompt changes.

IMP007: Reconcile the scope wording in [run_exp16_plan_review.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/run_exp16_plan_review.py):4 with the final Experiment 17 scope so the runner, plan, and review target the same thing.
